sentences.zh: 建文初，召拜禮部侍郎兼翰林學士，與方孝孺同侍經筵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwen reign, he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Rites concurrently Hanlin Academician, and together with Fang Xiaoru attended the lecture hall.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianwen reign he was called to court and made Vice Minister of Rites while also serving as a Hanlin academician, sharing duty at the imperial lectures with Fang Xiaoru.

sentences.zh: 禦書「怡老堂」額寵之，又賜髹幾、玉鳩杖。

translations.literal: The Emperor wrote in his own hand the plaque "Hall of Gentle Aging" as a mark of favor, and also bestowed a lacquered armrest and a jade dove-headed staff.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor honored him with an imperial inscription for the hall name "Hall of Gentle Aging," and further granted a lacquered reading desk and a jade-headed dove staff.

sentences.zh: 解縉謫河州，以倫言得召還。

translations.literal: Xie Jin was banished to Hezhou; on Lun's word he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Jin was exiled to Hezhou, it was on Lun's recommendation that he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 倫質直敦厚，嘗勸帝睦親藩，不聽。

translations.literal: Lun was plain, sincere, and thick and steady; he once urged the Emperor to keep peace with the imperial clansmen, but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was straightforward and steadfast by nature; he once urged the emperor to reconcile with the princely domains, but his counsel went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，倫年已八十，命致仕，尋卒。

translations.literal: When Chengzu took the throne, Lun was already eighty; he was ordered to retire, and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongle Emperor came to the throne, Lun was already eighty; he was ordered to retire from office and died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 其與倫同時為禮部侍郎者，有王景，字景彰，松陽人。

translations.literal: One who at the same time as Lun served as Vice Minister of Rites was Wang Jing, styled Jingzhang, a native of Songyang.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as Vice Minister of Rites at the same time as Lun was Wang Jing, whose style was Jingzhang and who came from Songyang.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，為懷遠教諭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Hongwu reign he was instructor at Huaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongwu reign he served as director of studies at Huaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 以博學應詔。

translations.literal: Because of broad learning he responded to the imperial summons.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court on account of his wide learning.

sentences.zh: 命作朝享樂章，定藩王朝覲儀。

translations.literal: He was ordered to compose music for the morning audience sacrifice and to fix the protocol for princely audiences at court.
translations.idiomatic: He was charged with composing the music for the morning court sacrifice and with setting the forms for princes attending audience.

sentences.zh: 累官山西參政，與倫先後謫雲南。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Shanxi Administrative Commissioner, and together with Lun was successively banished to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to become Administrative Commissioner of Shanxi, and he and Lun were banished to Yunnan in turn.

sentences.zh: 建文初，召入翰林，修《太祖實錄》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwen he was summoned into the Hanlin Academy to compile the Veritable Records of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianwen reign he was called into the Hanlin Academy to help compile the Veritable Records of the founding emperor.

sentences.zh: 用張紞薦，除禮部侍郎兼翰林侍講。

translations.literal: On Zhang Dan's recommendation he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites concurrently Hanlin Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: On Zhang Dan's recommendation he was made Vice Minister of Rites while also serving as a Hanlin lecturer.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，擢學士。

translations.literal: When Chengzu took the throne, he was promoted to Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne, Jing was promoted to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 帝問葬建文帝禮，景頓首言：「宜用天子禮。」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked about the rites for burying the Jianwen Emperor; Jing bowed his head and said: "One should use the rites of a Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked what funeral rites should be used for the Jianwen emperor, Jing kowtowed and said, "The rites appropriate to a Son of Heaven should be used."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 永樂六年卒於官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongle he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the sixth year of the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 儀智，字居真，高密人。

translations.literal: Yi Zhi, styled Juzhen, was a native of Gaomi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Zhi, whose style was Juzhen, came from Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 洪武末，舉耆儒，授高密訓導，遷莘縣教諭。

translations.literal: At the end of Hongwu he was recommended as a venerable scholar, appointed Gaomi Instructor, and transferred to be Director of Studies at Shen County.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Hongwu reign he was nominated as a senior scholar, appointed instructor at Gaomi, and later transferred to serve as director of studies in Shen County.

sentences.zh: 擢知高郵州，課農興學，吏民愛之。

translations.literal: He was promoted to be prefect of Gaoyou, urged agriculture and revived learning, and officials and people loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to prefect of Gaoyou, he promoted farming and revived schools, and both officials and common people held him in affection.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年遷寶慶知府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle he was transferred to be prefect of Baqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongle he was transferred to serve as prefect of Baqing.

sentences.zh: 土人健悍，獨畏智，相戒不敢犯。

translations.literal: The native people were sturdy and fierce; they alone feared Zhi, and warned one another not to offend him.
translations.idiomatic: The local people were hardy and fierce, yet they feared Zhi alone and warned one another not to transgress against him.

sentences.zh: 召為右通政兼右中允。

translations.literal: He was summoned to be Right Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission concurrently Right Middle Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as Right Vice Commissioner of Transmission while also holding the post of Right Middle Assistant in the Heir Apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷湖廣右布政使。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Right Administrative Commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Right Administrative Commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 坐事謫役通州。

translations.literal: Because of an offense he was banished to labor at Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After an offense he was demoted to penal labor at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，湖廣都指揮使龔忠入見。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year, Gong Zhong, Regional Commander of Huguang, came to audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixth year, Gong Zhong, regional commander of Huguang, came to audience.

sentences.zh: 帝問湖湘間老儒，忠以智對。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked about old scholars between the lakes and Xiang; Zhong answered with Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked about elderly scholars in the Hunan region, and Zhong named Zhi.

sentences.zh: 即日召之。

translations.literal: That same day he was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was summoned the same day.

sentences.zh: 既至，拜禮部左侍郎。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was appointed Left Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: On his arrival he was appointed Left Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十一年元旦，日當食，尚書呂震請朝賀如常，智持不可。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the eleventh year the sun was due to undergo an eclipse; Minister Lu Zhen asked that court congratulations proceed as usual, but Zhi held that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the eleventh year an eclipse was due; Minister Lu Zhen asked that the court hold its usual congratulatory audience, but Zhi objected.

sentences.zh: 會左諭德楊士奇亦以為言，乃免賀如智議。

translations.literal: It happened that Left Tutor Yang Shiqi also spoke to the same effect, and so congratulations were waived as Zhi had urged.
translations.idiomatic: As it happened, Left Tutor Yang Shiqi spoke to the same effect, and the congratulatory audience was canceled in accordance with Zhi's view.

sentences.zh: 十四年詔吏部、翰林院擇耆儒侍太孫。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year an edict ordered the Ministry of Personnel and the Hanlin Academy to select venerable scholars to attend the heir apparent's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year an edict directed the Ministry of Personnel and the Hanlin Academy to choose senior scholars to attend the heir apparent's grandson.

sentences.zh: 士奇及蹇義首薦智。

translations.literal: Shiqi and Jian Yi were the first to recommend Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi and Jian Yi were the first to recommend Zhi.

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「吾嘗舉李繼鼎，大誤，悔無及。

translations.literal: The heir apparent said: "I once recommended Li Jiding—a great mistake, and regret beyond remedy.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent said, "I once recommended Li Jiding—a grave mistake, and there is no undoing it.

sentences.zh: 智誠端士，然老矣。」

translations.literal: Zhi is indeed an upright man, yet he is old."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi is truly an upright man, but he is old."

sentences.zh: 士奇頓首言：「智起家學官，明理守正。

translations.literal: Shiqi bowed his head and said: "Zhi rose from school offices; he understands principle and holds to rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi kowtowed and said, "Zhi began as a school official; he understands principle and holds to what is right.

sentences.zh: 雖耄，精神未衰。

translations.literal: Although aged, his spirit has not declined.
translations.idiomatic: Though advanced in years, his vigor has not waned.

sentences.zh: 廷臣中老成正大，無逾智者。」

translations.literal: Among court ministers who are aged, upright, and magnanimous, none surpasses Zhi."
translations.idiomatic: Among the ministers at court who are aged, upright, and magnanimous, none surpasses Zhi."

sentences.zh: 是日午朝，帝顧太子曰：「侍太孫講讀得人未？」

translations.literal: That day at the noon audience the Emperor turned to the heir apparent and said: "Have you found the right men to attend the heir apparent's grandson in lecture and study?"
translations.idiomatic: That day at the noon audience the emperor turned to the heir apparent and asked, "Have you found suitable men to lecture and tutor the heir apparent's grandson?"

sentences.zh: 太子對曰：「舉禮部侍郎儀智，議未決。」

translations.literal: The heir apparent answered: "I have put forward Vice Minister of Rites Yi Zhi, but the matter is not yet settled."
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent replied, "I have proposed Vice Minister of Rites Yi Zhi, but the decision is not yet settled."

sentences.zh: 帝喜曰：「智雖老，能直言，可用也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said with pleasure: "Though Zhi is old, he can speak plainly; he may be used."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said with pleasure, "Though Zhi is old, he speaks plainly; he can be used."

sentences.zh: 遂命輔導皇太孫。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered him to assist and instruct the heir apparent's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Zhi to tutor the heir apparent's grandson.

sentences.zh: 每進講書史，必反覆啟迪，以正心術為本。

translations.literal: Whenever he entered to lecture on books and histories, he unfailingly instructed again and again, taking the rectification of the mind as the root.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he lectured on the classics and histories, he would instruct him again and again, always making the cultivation of the mind the foundation.

sentences.zh: 十九年，年八十，致仕，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, at age eighty, he retired and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, at the age of eighty, he retired from office and died at home.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年贈太子少保，謚文簡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Wénjiǎn.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Hongxi reign he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Wénjiǎn.

sentences.zh: 季子銘，字子新。

translations.literal: His youngest son Ming, styled Zixin.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son, Ming, whose style was Zixin.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，以侍郎戴綸薦，授行在禮科給事中。

translations.literal: When the Xuande Emperor took the throne, on Vice Minister Dai Lun's recommendation he was appointed Supervising Secretary in the Rites Section at the traveling secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xuande emperor came to the throne, on Vice Minister Dai Lun's recommendation he was appointed supervising secretary in the Rites Section at the traveling secretariat.

sentences.zh: 九年秩滿，帝念智舊勞，改銘修撰。

translations.literal: In the ninth year his term expired; the Emperor, recalling Zhi's old service, changed Ming to Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired in the ninth year, the emperor, mindful of Zhi's long service, transferred Ming to the post of compiler.

sentences.zh: 正統三年預修宣廟《實錄》成，遷侍講，後改郕府長史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengtong, after taking part in compiling the Veritable Records of the Xuande temple and finishing, he was transferred to Lecturer, and later made Chief Administrator of the Prince of Cheng's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhengtong, after helping compile the Veritable Records of the Xuande emperor, he was promoted to lecturer and later made chief administrator of the Prince of Cheng's household.

sentences.zh: 郕王監國，視朝午門。

translations.literal: The Prince of Cheng supervised the state and held court at the Meridian Gate at noon.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Cheng supervised the state, he held court at the Meridian Gate at noon.

sentences.zh: 廷臣劾王振，叫號莫辨人聲。

translations.literal: Court ministers impeached Wang Zhen; shouting and clamor made human voices indistinguishable.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers impeached Wang Zhen, and the hall rang with such shouting that individual voices could not be distinguished.

sentences.zh: 銘獨造膝前，免冠敷奏。

translations.literal: Ming alone went before the knee, removed his cap, and laid out his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Ming alone went forward, removed his cap, and presented his memorial kneeling before the prince.

sentences.zh: 下令旨族振，眾嘩始息。

translations.literal: He issued an order to exterminate Zhen's clan, and only then did the uproar cease.
translations.idiomatic: He issued an order to execute Wang Zhen and his entire clan, and only then did the clamor subside.

sentences.zh: 景帝即位，力贊征伐諸大事。

translations.literal: When the Jingdi Emperor took the throne, he strongly supported the great affairs of campaigning and punitive expeditions.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingdi emperor came to the throne, Ming strongly supported the major campaigns and punitive expeditions.

sentences.zh: 尋以潛邸恩，授禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long, on account of favor from the hidden residence, he was appointed Right Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, as a reward for service in the prince's household before his accession, he was made Right Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 明年兼經筵官。

translations.literal: The next year he was additionally made an officer of the lecture hall.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was also appointed to the imperial lecture staff.

sentences.zh: 帝每臨講幄，輒命中官擲金錢於地，任講官遍拾之，號「恩典」。

translations.literal: Whenever the Emperor came to the lecture canopy, he would order eunuchs to cast coins on the ground and let the lecturers pick them up at will; this was called the "grace gift."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor attended the lecture pavilion, he would have eunuchs scatter coins on the ground for the lecturers to gather as they pleased—a practice known as the "grace gift."

sentences.zh: 文臣與者，內閣高谷等外，惟銘與俞山、俞綱、蕭鎡、趙琬數人而已。

translations.literal: Among civil officials who received it, apart from Grand Secretary Gao Gu and others in the Secretariat, only Ming together with Yu Shan, Yu Gang, Xiao Zi, and Zhao Wan were a mere few.
translations.idiomatic: Among civil officials who received it, apart from Grand Secretary Gao Gu and others in the inner court, only Ming together with Yu Shan, Yu Gang, Xiao Zi, and Zhao Wan numbered among the few.

sentences.zh: 尋進南京禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was advanced to Minister of Rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Minister of Rites at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 懷獻太子立，加太子太保，召為兵部尚書兼詹事。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent Huai Xian was established, he was given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and summoned to be Minister of War concurrently Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent Huai Xian was installed, Ming was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and summoned to serve as Minister of War while also holding the post of Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 蘇州、淮安諸郡積雪，民凍餓死相枕。

translations.literal: In Suzhou, Huai'an, and other prefectures snow piled up; the people died of cold and hunger lying one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow fell in Suzhou, Huai'an, and other prefectures, and the people died of cold and hunger in heaps.

sentences.zh: 沙灣築河，役山東、河南九萬人，責民間鐵器數萬具。

translations.literal: At Shawan a river dike was built, employing ninety thousand men from Shandong and Henan, and demanding tens of thousands of iron implements from the populace.
translations.idiomatic: At Shawan a river embankment was built, conscripting ninety thousand men from Shandong and Henan and levying tens of thousands of iron tools from the populace.

sentences.zh: 銘請於帝，多所寬恤。

translations.literal: Ming petitioned the Emperor, and in many matters relief and leniency were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Ming appealed to the emperor, and in many matters leniency was granted.

sentences.zh: 因災異，言消弭在敬天法祖，省刑薄斂，節用愛人。

translations.literal: Because of calamities and prodigies, he said that dispelling them lay in revering Heaven and following the ancestors, reducing punishments and lightening levies, and being frugal and cherishing the people.
translations.idiomatic: In view of omens and disasters, he said that their removal lay in revering Heaven and honoring the ancestors, reducing punishments and lightening taxes, and practicing frugality while caring for the people.

sentences.zh: 錄《皇明祖訓錄》以進，深見獎納。

translations.literal: He compiled the Record of the Ancestral Instructions of the Great Ming and presented it, and was deeply praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled and presented the Record of the Ancestral Instructions of the Great Ming and was warmly praised and rewarded.

sentences.zh: 卒，謚忠襄。

translations.literal: He died, with the posthumous title Zhōngxiāng.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Zhōngxiāng.

sentences.zh: 銘少學於吳訥。

translations.literal: Ming in youth studied under Wu Na.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Ming studied under Wu Na.

sentences.zh: 天性孝友，易直有父風。

translations.literal: By nature he was filial and friendly; easy and direct, he had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was filial and brotherly; open and direct, he bore his father's manner.

sentences.zh: 長子海，錦衣衛百戶。

translations.literal: His eldest son Hai was a company commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Hai served as a company commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 季子泰，舉於鄉，為禮科給事中。

translations.literal: His youngest son Tai was successful in the provincial examination and served as Supervising Secretary in the Rites Section.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Tai passed the provincial examination and served as supervising secretary in the Rites Section.

sentences.zh: 並以父恩授雲。

translations.literal: Both received appointment through their father's grace.
translations.idiomatic: Both received office through their father's favor.

sentences.zh: 鄒濟，字汝舟，余杭人。

translations.literal: Zou Ji, styled Ruzhou, was a native of Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Ji, whose style was Ruzhou, came from Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: He was known for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He was renowned for the filial care with which he served his mother.

sentences.zh: 博學強記，尤長《春秋》。

translations.literal: Broadly learned with a strong memory, he was especially skilled in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned and with a powerful memory, he was especially accomplished in the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 為余杭訓導，師法嚴。

translations.literal: He was Yuhang Instructor, strict in teaching method.
translations.idiomatic: As instructor at Yuhang he was strict in his teaching.

sentences.zh: 累遷國子學錄、助教，以薦知平度州。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Recorder and Assistant Instructor in the Directorate of Education, and on recommendation became prefect of Pingdu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of recorder and assistant instructor in the Directorate of Education, and on recommendation was appointed prefect of Pingdu.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，預修《太祖實錄》成，除禮部郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle, after taking part in compiling the Veritable Records of Taizu and finishing, he was appointed Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongle reign, after helping compile the Veritable Records of the founding emperor, he was appointed a director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 征安南，從幕府司奏記。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Annam he followed the staff headquarters as recorder of memorials.
translations.idiomatic: On the expedition against Annam he served on the campaign staff as recorder of memorials.

sentences.zh: 還為廣東右參政，再遷左春坊左庶子，授皇孫經。

translations.literal: On his return he became Right Administrative Commissioner of Guangdong, was again transferred to Left Sub-Tutor in the Left Quarters of the Heir Apparent's Household, and instructed the emperor's grandson in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Right Administrative Commissioner of Guangdong, then transferred to Left Sub-Tutor in the heir apparent's household, where he lectured the emperor's grandson on the classics.

sentences.zh: 濟為人和易坦夷，無貴賤皆樂親之。

translations.literal: Ji was by nature easy and open, plain and unassuming; whether noble or base, all were glad to be close to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was easygoing and open by nature; high and low alike were glad to draw near him.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，進少詹事。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was advanced to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 當是時，宮僚多得罪，徐善述、王汝玉、馬京、梁潛輩被讒，相繼下獄死。

translations.literal: At that time many household officers fell into guilt; Xu Shanshu, Wang Ruyu, Ma Jing, Liang Qian, and their like were slandered and in succession imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many officers of the heir apparent's household fell from favor; Xu Shanshu, Wang Ruyu, Ma Jing, Liang Qian, and others were slandered and died one after another in prison.

sentences.zh: 濟積憂得疾。

translations.literal: Ji accumulated worry and fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Ji fell ill from accumulated grief.

sentences.zh: 皇太子以書慰曰：「卿善自攝。

translations.literal: The heir apparent sent a letter to comfort him, saying: "Take good care of yourself.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent wrote to comfort him, saying, "Take good care of yourself.

sentences.zh: 即有不諱，當提攜卿息，不使墜蓬蒿也。」

translations.literal: If anything untoward should occur, I shall support your sons and not let them fall into the weeds."
translations.idiomatic: Should the worst befall, I shall look after your sons and not let them sink into obscurity."

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年贈太子少保，謚文敏。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Wénmǐn.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Hongxi reign he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Wénmǐn.

sentences.zh: 命有司立祠墓側，春秋祀之。

translations.literal: An order was given to the authorities to erect a shrine beside his tomb and sacrifice to him in spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities were ordered to erect a shrine beside his tomb and offer sacrifices in spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 子幹，字宗盛，濟卒時尚幼。

translations.literal: His son Gan, styled Zongsheng, was still young when Ji died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gan, whose style was Zongsheng, was still a child when Ji died.

sentences.zh: 仁宗監國，命為應天府學生，月賜鈔米。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor supervised the state, he was ordered to be a student at the Yingtian Prefecture school, with paper money and grain granted monthly.
translations.idiomatic: When the Renzong emperor supervised the state, Gan was enrolled as a student at the Yingtian prefectural school and granted paper money and grain each month.

sentences.zh: 舉正統四年進士。

translations.literal: He was successful as a presented scholar in the fourth year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fourth year of Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 景帝初，由兵部郎中超擢本部右侍郎，以才為于謙所倚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingdi reign, from Director in the Ministry of War he was abruptly promoted to Right Vice Minister of the same ministry, and for his talent was relied on by Yu Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingdi reign he was abruptly promoted from director in the Ministry of War to Right Vice Minister of the same ministry, and Yu Qian relied on his ability.

sentences.zh: 也先入寇，九門皆閉。

translations.literal: When the Oirats invaded, the Nine Gates were all closed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Oirats invaded, all nine gates of the capital were shut.

sentences.zh: 百姓避兵者，號城下求入，幹開門納之。

translations.literal: Common people fleeing the troops cried beneath the walls begging to enter; Gan opened the gates and admitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Common people fleeing the fighting cried beneath the walls to be let in, and Gan opened the gates to admit them.

sentences.zh: 尋改禮部，兼庶子，考察山西官吏，黜布政使侯復以下五十余人。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites, concurrently Sub-Tutor, inspected officials in Shanxi, and dismissed more than fifty persons including Administrative Commissioner Hou Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites while also serving as sub-tutor; he inspected officials in Shanxi and dismissed more than fifty men, including Administrative Commissioner Hou Fu.

sentences.zh: 巡視河南、鳳陽水災，與王竑請振。

translations.literal: He toured flood disasters in Henan and Fengyang, and together with Wang Hong requested relief.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected flood damage in Henan and Fengyang and, together with Wang Hong, petitioned for relief.

sentences.zh: 又請令諸生輸粟入監讀書。

translations.literal: He also asked that students be allowed to present grain and enter the Directorate of Education to study.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned that students be allowed to present grain and enter the Directorate of Education to study.

sentences.zh: 納粟入監自此始。

translations.literal: Admission to the Directorate by presenting grain began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Admission to the Directorate by presenting grain began from this time.

sentences.zh: 成化二年振畿內饑，再遷禮部尚書，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua he relieved famine within the capital region, was again transferred to Minister of Rites, and given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chenghua he relieved famine in the capital region, was again promoted to Minister of Rites, and made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 被劾乞休，卒，謚康靖。

translations.literal: Impeached, he begged to retire; he died, with the posthumous title Kāngjìng.
translations.idiomatic: After impeachment he petitioned to retire; he died and was given the posthumous title Kāngjìng.

sentences.zh: 徐善述，字好古，天臺人。

translations.literal: Xu Shanshu, styled Haogu, was a native of Tiantai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shanshu, whose style was Haogu, came from Tiantai.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，行歲貢法，善述首貢入太學。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu reign the annual tribute student system was implemented; Shanshu was the first tribute student to enter the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu reign the annual tribute-student system was introduced, and Shanshu was the first tribute student to enter the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 授桂陽州學正。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of Studies at Guiyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director of studies at Guiyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，以國子博士擢春坊司直郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle, from Doctor of the Directorate of Education he was promoted to Rectifier in the Eastern Quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongle reign he was promoted from doctor in the Directorate of Education to rectifier in the Eastern Quarters of the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 見重於皇太子，每稱為「先生」，嘗致書賜酒及詩。

translations.literal: He was valued by the heir apparent, who always called him "Master," and once sent a letter bestowing wine and a poem.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent held him in high regard, always addressing him as "Master," and once sent him a letter with gifts of wine and a poem.

sentences.zh: 遷左贊善，坐累死。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Tutor and died in prison from overwork.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Left Tutor and died in prison from overwork.

sentences.zh: 與鄒濟同日贈太子少師，謚文肅。

translations.literal: On the same day as Zou Ji he was posthumously made Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Wénsù.
translations.idiomatic: On the same day as Zou Ji he was posthumously made Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Wénsù.

sentences.zh: 立祠，春秋祀亦如濟。

translations.literal: A shrine was erected, and spring and autumn sacrifices were offered as for Ji.
translations.idiomatic: A shrine was erected for him, with spring and autumn sacrifices as for Ji.

sentences.zh: 王汝玉，名遂，以字行，長洲人。

translations.literal: Wang Ruyu, personal name Sui, was known by his style; he was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ruyu, whose personal name was Sui but who was known by his style, came from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 穎敏強記。

translations.literal: Quick and keen, with a strong memory.
translations.idiomatic: He was quick-witted and possessed a powerful memory.

sentences.zh: 少從楊維楨學。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Yang Weizhen.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he studied under Yang Weizhen.

sentences.zh: 年十七，舉於鄉。

translations.literal: At age seventeen he was successful in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，由應天府學訓導擢翰林五經博士，歷遷右春坊右贊善，預修《永樂大典》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle, from Instructor at the Yingtian Prefecture school he was promoted to Hanlin Doctor of the Five Classics, was successively transferred to Right Tutor in the Right Quarters, and took part in compiling the Yongle Encyclopedia.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongle reign he was promoted from instructor at the Yingtian school to Hanlin Doctor of the Five Classics, rose to Right Tutor in the heir apparent's household, and helped compile the Yongle Encyclopedia.

sentences.zh: 仁宗在東宮，特被寵遇。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor was in the Eastern Palace, he was especially favored.
translations.idiomatic: When the Renzong emperor was heir apparent, Ruyu enjoyed special favor.

sentences.zh: 群臣應制撰《神龜賦》，汝玉第一，解縉次之。

translations.literal: The ministers composed on command the "Fu on the Divine Tortoise"; Ruyu ranked first and Xie Jin second.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministers composed on imperial command the "Rhapsody on the Divine Tortoise," Ruyu ranked first and Xie Jin second.

sentences.zh: 七年坐修《禮書》紊制度，當戍邊。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, because in compiling the Book of Rites he disturbed the institutional order, he was due for frontier garrison service.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was sentenced to frontier garrison duty for having disturbed institutional order while compiling the Book of Rites.

sentences.zh: 皇太子監國，宥之，以為翰林典籍。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent supervised the state, he pardoned him and made him a Hanlin Archivist.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent supervised the state, he pardoned Ruyu and appointed him a Hanlin archivist.

sentences.zh: 尋進左贊善，坐解縉累，瘐死。

translations.literal: Before long he was advanced to Left Tutor; implicated through Xie Jin, he died of illness in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Left Tutor; implicated in Xie Jin's case, he died of illness in confinement.

sentences.zh: 洪熙初，贈太子賓客，謚文靖，遣官祭其家。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongxi he was posthumously made Guest of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Wénjìng, and officials were sent to sacrifice at his home.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongxi reign he was posthumously made Guest of the Heir Apparent, given the posthumous title Wénjìng, and officials were sent to offer sacrifices at his home.

sentences.zh: 子楘，由進士為刑部主事，善辨冤獄。

translations.literal: His son Mo, through the presented scholar degree, became a Principal Clerk in the Ministry of Punishments and was skilled at distinguishing wrongful cases.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mo, a presented scholar, served as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments and was skilled at clearing wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 用薦擢廣西副使，進布政使。

translations.literal: On recommendation he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of Guangxi and advanced to Administrative Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation he was promoted to vice commissioner of Guangxi and later to administrative commissioner.

sentences.zh: 將士多殺良民報功，楘諭其帥，生致難民一人，準功一級，全活無算。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers often killed good common people to report merit; Mo instructed their commanders that for each refugee delivered alive one grade of merit would be allowed, and countless lives were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers often killed innocent civilians to claim merit; Mo instructed their commanders that for each refugee delivered alive one grade of merit would be credited, saving countless lives.

sentences.zh: 田州土官岑鑒兄弟相仇，楘為解之，卻其厚饋。

translations.literal: The native officials of Tianzhou, the brothers Cen Jian, were at feud with one another; Mo settled it for them and declined their lavish gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The native officials of Tianzhou, the brothers Cen Jian, were at feud; Mo reconciled them and declined their lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 撫服梗化女土官，民夷服其信義。

translations.literal: He pacified and won over a recalcitrant female native official; common people and tribes submitted to his faith and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified a recalcitrant female native official, and both Chinese and tribal peoples submitted to his integrity.

sentences.zh: 終浙江布政使。

translations.literal: He ended as Administrative Commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Administrative Commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 周述，字崇述，吉水人。

translations.literal: Zhou Shu, styled Chongshu, was a native of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shu, whose style was Chongshu, came from Jishui.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年與從弟孟簡並進士及第。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle he and his younger cousin Meng Jian together passed the presented scholar examination with highest honors.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongle he and his younger cousin Meng Jian both passed the metropolitan examination with highest honors.

sentences.zh: 帝手題二人策，獎賞之，並授翰林編修。

translations.literal: The Emperor wrote in his own hand on the two men's examination answers, rewarded them, and together appointed them Hanlin Compilers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor inscribed commendations in his own hand on their examination papers, rewarded them, and appointed them both Hanlin compilers.

sentences.zh: 尋詔解縉選曾棨等二十八人讀書文淵閣，述、孟簡皆與焉。

translations.literal: Before long an edict ordered Xie Jin to select Zeng Qi and twenty-eight others to study in the Wenyuan Pavilion; Shu and Meng Jian were both among them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict directed Xie Jin to select Zeng Qi and twenty-eight others to study in the Wenyuan Pavilion; Shu and Meng Jian were both included.

sentences.zh: 司禮監給紙筆，光祿給朝暮饌，禮部月給膏燭鈔人三錠，工部擇近宅居之，一時以為榮。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Ceremonies supplied paper and brushes, the Court of Imperial Entertainments supplied morning and evening meals, the Ministry of Rites monthly supplied lamp oil, candles, and three ingots of paper money per person, and the Ministry of Works chose a nearby residence for them to dwell in; for a time this was regarded as glory.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Ceremonies supplied paper and brushes, the Court of Imperial Entertainments provided morning and evening meals, the Ministry of Rites granted lamp oil, candles, and three ingots of paper money per person each month, and the Ministry of Works chose a nearby residence for them—all regarded at the time as a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 述嘗扈北巡，累進左春坊諭德。

translations.literal: Shu once followed the northern tour as attendant, and was successively promoted to Instructor in the Left Quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Shu once accompanied the northern tour and was successively promoted to instructor in the Left Quarters of the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，命從皇太子謁陵南京。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor took the throne, he was ordered to follow the heir apparent in paying respects at the tombs in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Renzong emperor came to the throne, Shu was ordered to accompany the heir apparent to the imperial tombs at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 召至榻前，問所以匡弼儲君者，對稱旨。

translations.literal: He was summoned before the couch and asked how he would assist and correct the heir apparent; his answer pleased the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned before the emperor's couch, he was asked how he would guide the heir apparent; his answer pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 宣宗時，進左庶子。

translations.literal: In the Xuande reign he was advanced to Left Sub-Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Xuande emperor he was promoted to Left Sub-Tutor.

sentences.zh: 正統初，卒官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengtong he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengtong reign he died in office.

sentences.zh: 孟簡在翰林二十年，始遷詹事府丞，出為襄王府長史。

translations.literal: Meng Jian was in the Hanlin Academy twenty years before he was first transferred to Vice Director of the Household of the Heir Apparent, and went out to be Chief Administrator of the Prince of Xiang's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Jian spent twenty years in the Hanlin Academy before he was first transferred to vice director of the heir apparent's household and then sent out as chief administrator of the Prince of Xiang's establishment.

sentences.zh: 有言宜留備顧問者，帝曰：「輔朕弟，尤勝於輔朕也。」

translations.literal: Some said he ought to be kept as a reserve adviser; the Emperor said: "To assist my younger brother is even better than assisting me."
translations.idiomatic: When some said he ought to be kept as a court adviser, the emperor said, "To assist my younger brother is even better than assisting me."

sentences.zh: 述溫厚簡靜，未嘗有疾言遽色，文章雅贍。

translations.literal: Shu was warm, thick, simple, and quiet; he never had harsh words or a sudden countenance, and his writings were elegant and ample.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was warm and restrained, never speaking harshly or showing sudden anger, and his writings were elegant and ample.

sentences.zh: 孟簡謙退不伐，生平無睚眥於人。

translations.literal: Meng Jian was modest and retiring without boasting; in his life he bore no grudge against anyone.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Jian was modest and unassuming, bearing no grudge against anyone in his life.

sentences.zh: 並為世所重雲。

translations.literal: Both were highly regarded by the age, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Both were highly regarded in their time.

sentences.zh: 陳濟，字伯載，武進人。

translations.literal: Chen Ji, styled Bozai, was a native of Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ji, whose style was Bozai, came from Wujin.

sentences.zh: 讀書過目成誦。

translations.literal: In reading, what passed before his eyes he could recite.
translations.idiomatic: What he read once he could recite from memory.

sentences.zh: 嘗以父命如錢塘，家人賫貨以從。

translations.literal: Once on his father's orders he went to Qiantang; the household sent goods to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Once, on his father's orders, he went to Qiantang, and the household sent goods for him to carry.

sentences.zh: 比還，以其貲之半市書，口誦手鈔。

translations.literal: When he returned, he used half the goods to buy books, reciting aloud and copying by hand.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he spent half the goods on books, reciting aloud and copying them by hand.

sentences.zh: 十余年，盡通經史百家之言。

translations.literal: In more than ten years he thoroughly mastered the words of the classics, histories, and the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: In little more than ten years he mastered the classics, histories, and the writings of the hundred schools.

sentences.zh: 成祖詔修《永樂大典》，用大臣薦，以布衣召為都總裁，修撰曾棨等為之副。

translations.literal: Chengzu ordered the compilation of the Yongle Encyclopedia; on a great minister's recommendation he was summoned as a commoner to be Chief General Editor, with Compilers such as Zeng Qi as his deputies.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle emperor ordered the compilation of the Yongle Encyclopedia; on a senior minister's recommendation Ji was summoned from private life to serve as chief general editor, with compilers such as Zeng Qi as his deputies.

sentences.zh: 詞臣纂修者，及太學儒生數千人，繙秘庫書數百萬卷，浩無端倪。

translations.literal: Literary officials who compiled and revised, together with several thousand Confucian students of the Imperial Academy, turned through several million volumes from the secret archives, vast without limit or clue.
translations.idiomatic: Literary officials who compiled the work, together with several thousand students of the Imperial Academy, turned through millions of volumes from the secret archives—a task vast beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 濟與少師姚廣孝等數人，發凡起例，區分鉤考，秩然有法。

translations.literal: Ji together with Junior Preceptor Yao Guangxiao and a few others set forth principles and established categories, divided and collated, and brought order with method.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, together with Junior Preceptor Yao Guangxiao and a few others, laid down principles and categories, divided and collated the material, and imposed a clear method on the work.

sentences.zh: 執筆者有所疑，輒就濟質問，應口辨析無滯。

translations.literal: Whenever those who held the brush had doubts, they would go to Ji to question him; he answered from the mouth, analyzing without obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever those drafting the work had doubts, they would consult Ji, who answered on the spot without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 書成，授右贊善。

translations.literal: When the book was finished, he was appointed Right Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When the compilation was finished, he was appointed Right Tutor.

sentences.zh: 謹慎無過，皇太子甚禮重之。

translations.literal: Careful and cautious without fault, the heir apparent greatly honored and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Careful and without fault, he was greatly honored by the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 凡稽古纂集之事，悉以屬濟。

translations.literal: All matters of investigating antiquity and compiling collections were entirely entrusted to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: All matters of historical research and compilation were entrusted entirely to Ji.

sentences.zh: 隨事敷奏，多所裨益。

translations.literal: As affairs arose he laid them out in memorials, and in many matters was of benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on affairs as they arose and was of great benefit in many matters.

sentences.zh: 五皇孫皆從受經。

translations.literal: All five of the emperor's grandsons received the classics from him.
translations.idiomatic: All five of the emperor's grandsons studied the classics under him.

sentences.zh: 居職十五年而卒。

translations.literal: He held office fifteen years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He held office for fifteen years and then died.

sentences.zh: 年六十二。

translations.literal: He was sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty-two years old.

sentences.zh: 濟少有酒過，母戒之，終其身未嘗至醉。

translations.literal: Ji in youth had a fault of wine; his mother admonished him, and to the end of his life he never reached drunkenness.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Ji had a weakness for wine; his mother admonished him, and he never became truly drunk in his life.

sentences.zh: 弟洽為兵部尚書，事濟如父。

translations.literal: His younger brother Qia was Minister of War and served Ji as to a father.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Qia served as Minister of War and treated Ji as he would a father.

sentences.zh: 濟深懼盛滿，彌自謙抑。

translations.literal: Ji deeply feared fullness at the height of fortune and all the more restrained himself in humility.
translations.idiomatic: Ji deeply feared the dangers of eminence and became all the more self-restrained and humble.

sentences.zh: 所居蓬戶葦壁，裁蔽風雨，終日危坐，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: Where he dwelt had a wicker gate and reed walls, barely sheltering from wind and rain; all day he sat upright, his hand never releasing a scroll.
translations.idiomatic: He lived behind a wicker gate and reed walls that barely kept out wind and rain; all day he sat upright, never setting down his books.

sentences.zh: 為文根據經史，不事葩藻。

translations.literal: In writing he rooted himself in the classics and histories and did not pursue ornament.
translations.idiomatic: His writing was grounded in the classics and histories and avoided ornamental flourish.

sentences.zh: 嘗云：「文貴如布帛菽粟，有益於世爾。」

translations.literal: He once said: "Writing is prized like cloth, silk, beans, and grain—only in benefiting the age."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Writing should be valued like cloth, silk, beans, and grain—only insofar as it benefits the world."

sentences.zh: 其後有陳繼、楊翥者，亦以布衣通經。

translations.literal: Afterward there were Chen Ji and Yang Chong, who also as commoners mastered the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Later there were Chen Ji and Yang Chong, who likewise mastered the classics as men in private life.

sentences.zh: 用楊士奇薦，繼由博士入翰林。

translations.literal: On Yang Shiqi's recommendation, Ji entered the Hanlin Academy from the post of Doctor.
translations.idiomatic: On Yang Shiqi's recommendation, Chen Ji entered the Hanlin Academy from a doctorate in the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 而翥竟用景帝潛邸恩，與俞山、俞綱等皆至大官。

translations.literal: But Chong ultimately used favor from the Jingdi Emperor's hidden residence, and together with Yu Shan, Yu Gang, and others all reached high office.
translations.idiomatic: Chong, however, rose through favor earned in the Jingdi emperor's household before his accession, and he, Yu Shan, Yu Gang, and others all reached high office.

sentences.zh: 自天順後，始漸拘資格。

translations.literal: From after the Tianshun reign, qualifications began gradually to be strictly observed.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the Tianshun reign did the court gradually begin to enforce formal qualifications.

sentences.zh: 編修馬升、檢討傅宗不由科目，李賢皆出之為參議。

translations.literal: Compilers Ma Sheng and Reviser Fu Zong did not come through the examination curriculum; Li Xian all sent them out as Administrative Commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: The compilers Ma Sheng and Fu Zong had not come up through the examination system; Li Xian transferred them all to posts as administrative commissioners.

sentences.zh: 布衣無得預館閣者，而弘治間潘辰獨以才望得之，一時詫異數焉。

translations.literal: Commoners could not gain entry to the Academy and Pavilion, but in the Hongzhi reign Pan Chen alone obtained it through talent and reputation, and for a time this was marveled at as a rare case.
translations.idiomatic: Men in private life could no longer enter the Hanlin Academy, yet in the Hongzhi reign Pan Chen alone gained admission through talent and reputation—a rare exception at the time.

sentences.zh: 楊翥，字仲舉，亦吳人。

translations.literal: Yang Chong, styled Zhongju, was also a man of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chong, whose style was Zhongju, was also from Wu.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，隨兄戍武昌，授徒自給。

translations.literal: Orphaned and poor in youth, he followed his elder brother on garrison duty at Wuchang and supported himself by teaching pupils.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in his youth, he followed his elder brother to garrison duty at Wuchang and supported himself by teaching.

sentences.zh: 楊士奇微時，流寄窘乏，翥輒解館舍讓之，而己教授他所。

translations.literal: When Yang Shiqi was in humble circumstances, drifting and lodged in want, Chong would yield his lodging to him and himself teach elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Shiqi was still obscure and living in hardship, Chong would give up his lodging for him and teach elsewhere himself.

sentences.zh: 士奇心賢之。

translations.literal: Shiqi in his heart regarded him as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi admired him in his heart.

sentences.zh: 及貴，薦翥經明行修。

translations.literal: When he became eminent, he recommended Chong as clear in the classics and cultivated in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When he rose to eminence, he recommended Chong as learned in the classics and upright in conduct.

sentences.zh: 宣宗詔試吏部，稱旨，授翰林院檢討，歷修撰。

translations.literal: The Xuande Emperor ordered him tested at the Ministry of Personnel; he pleased the intent and was appointed Reviser in the Hanlin Academy, and rose through Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuande emperor ordered him examined by the Ministry of Personnel; he pleased the emperor and was appointed Hanlin reviser, later rising to compiler.

sentences.zh: 正統中，詔簡郕王府僚。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong reign an edict selected staff for the Prince of Cheng's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign an edict called for selection of staff for the Prince of Cheng's household.

sentences.zh: 諸翰林皆不欲行，乃出侍講儀銘及翥為左右長史。

translations.literal: All the Hanlin scholars were unwilling to go; thereupon Lecturer Yi Ming and Chong were sent out as Left and Right Chief Administrators.
translations.idiomatic: None of the Hanlin scholars wished to go; accordingly Lecturer Yi Ming and Chong were sent out as left and right chief administrators.

sentences.zh: 久之，引年歸。

translations.literal: After a long time he cited age and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he cited his age and retired.

sentences.zh: 王即大位，入朝，拜禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Prince took the great position, he entered court and was appointed Right Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince came to the throne, Chong entered court and was appointed Right Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年進尚書，給祿致仕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingtai he was advanced to Minister and granted salary while retiring.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jingtai he was promoted to minister and retired on full salary.

sentences.zh: 明年卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: The next year he died at age eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 翥篤行絕俗，一時縉紳厚德者，翥為最。

translations.literal: Chong's conduct was earnest and apart from the vulgar; among gentry and officials of the time who were thick in virtue, Chong was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's conduct was earnest and far above the common run; among the cultivated officials of his day who were noted for moral weight, he stood foremost.

sentences.zh: 既沒，景帝念之，召其子聿入覲，授本邑主簿。

translations.literal: After his death the Jingdi Emperor remembered him, summoned his son Yu to audience, and appointed him chief clerk of his native district.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the Jingdi emperor remembered him, summoned his son Yu to audience, and appointed him chief clerk of his native district.

sentences.zh: 俞山，字積之，秀水人。

translations.literal: Yu Shan, styled Jizhi, was a native of Xiushui.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shan, whose style was Jizhi, came from Xiushui.

sentences.zh: 由鄉舉為郕府伴讀。

translations.literal: Through the provincial recommendation he became a study companion in the Prince of Cheng's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Through the provincial examination he became a study companion in the Prince of Cheng's household.

sentences.zh: 景帝時，拜吏部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Jingdi reign he was appointed Right Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jingdi emperor he was appointed Right Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 而嘉興俞綱由諸生繕寫《實錄》，試中書舍人，授郕府審理。

translations.literal: But Yu Gang of Jiaxing, from a student copying the Veritable Records, passed the examination for Secretariat Drafter and was appointed Adjudicator in the Prince of Cheng's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gang of Jiaxing, however, had begun as a student copying the Veritable Records, passed the examination for secretariat drafter, and was appointed adjudicator in the Prince of Cheng's household.

sentences.zh: 景帝時，以兵部右侍郎入閣預機務。

translations.literal: In the Jingdi reign, as Right Vice Minister of War he entered the Secretariat to take part in confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jingdi emperor he entered the inner court as Right Vice Minister of War to take part in state deliberations.

sentences.zh: 居三日，固辭，守本官。

translations.literal: After three days he firmly declined and kept his original office.
translations.idiomatic: After three days he firmly declined and retained his original post.

sentences.zh: 景帝將易東宮，山密疏諫。

translations.literal: When the Jingdi Emperor was about to change the Eastern Palace, Shan sent a secret memorial remonstrating.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingdi emperor planned to replace the heir apparent, Shan submitted a secret memorial in protest.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: His counsel went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 懷獻太子立，加太子少傅，山意不自安，致仕去。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent Huai Xian was established, Shan was given the additional title Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; he felt ill at ease and retired.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent Huai Xian was installed, Shan was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, but he felt uneasy and retired from office.

sentences.zh: 綱加太子少保。

translations.literal: Gang was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Gang was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，山以致仕得免。

translations.literal: When the Yingzong Emperor restored the throne, Shan escaped harm because he had already retired.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yingzong emperor regained the throne, Shan escaped punishment because he had already retired.

sentences.zh: 而綱當景泰時，能周旋二帝間，故得調南京禮部。

translations.literal: But Gang, during the Jingtai reign, was able to move between the two emperors, and therefore was transferred to the Ministry of Rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Gang, however, had managed to navigate between the two emperors during the Jingtai reign and was therefore transferred to the Ministry of Rites at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 成化初致仕，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua he retired and died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chenghua reign he retired and died.

sentences.zh: 潘辰，字時用，景寧人。

translations.literal: Pan Chen, styled Shiyong, was a native of Jingning.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Chen, whose style was Shiyong, came from Jingning.

sentences.zh: 少孤，隨從父家京師，以文學名。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he followed his uncle's family to the capital and was known for literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in his youth, he went with his uncle's family to the capital and became known for his literary accomplishments.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年詔天下舉才德之士隱於山林者。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongzhi an edict ordered the realm to recommend men of talent and virtue hidden in mountains and forests.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Hongzhi an edict called on the empire to recommend talented and virtuous men living in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 府尹唐恂舉辰，吏部以辰生長京師，寢之。

translations.literal: Prefect Tang Xun recommended Chen; the Ministry of Personnel, because Chen had grown up in the capital, shelved it.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Tang Xun recommended Chen, but the Ministry of Personnel shelved the nomination because Chen had grown up in the capital.

sentences.zh: 恂復奏，給事中王綸、夏昂亦交章薦，乃授翰林待詔。

translations.literal: Xun memorialized again; Supervising Secretaries Wang Lun and Xia Ang also submitted successive memorials recommending him, and he was appointed Hanlin Awaiting Edict.
translations.idiomatic: Xun memorialized again, and Supervising Secretaries Wang Lun and Xia Ang also submitted joint recommendations, whereupon Chen was appointed a Hanlin awaiting-edict.

sentences.zh: 久之，掌典籍事。

translations.literal: After a long time he was put in charge of archival matters.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was put in charge of the archives.

sentences.zh: 預修《會典》成，進五經博士。

translations.literal: After taking part in compiling the Collected Statutes and finishing, he was advanced to Doctor of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: After helping compile the Collected Statutes he was promoted to Doctor of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 正德中，劉瑾摘《會典》小疵，復降為典籍，俄還故官。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde reign Liu Jin seized on minor flaws in the Collected Statutes, and Chen was again demoted to Archivist; before long he returned to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign Liu Jin seized on minor flaws in the Collected Statutes, and Chen was demoted again to archivist, but soon regained his former post.

sentences.zh: 南京缺祭酒，吏部推石缶及辰。

translations.literal: Nanjing lacked a Chancellor of the Directorate of Education; the Ministry of Personnel recommended Shi Fou and Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing lacked a chancellor of the Directorate of Education, the Ministry of Personnel recommended Shi Fou and Chen.

sentences.zh: 帝以命缶，而擢辰編修。

translations.literal: The Emperor appointed Fou, and promoted Chen to Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Fou, but promoted Chen to compiler.

sentences.zh: 居九年，超擢太常少卿，致仕歸，卒。

translations.literal: After nine years he was abruptly promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, retired and returned home, and died.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years he was abruptly promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, retired home, and died.

sentences.zh: 特賜祭葬。

translations.literal: He was specially granted sacrificial burial.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially granted an imperial funeral sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 辰居官勤慎，晨入夜歸。

translations.literal: In office Chen was diligent and cautious, entering at dawn and returning at night.
translations.idiomatic: In office Chen was diligent and careful, arriving at dawn and leaving at night.

sentences.zh: 典制誥時，有以幣酬者，堅卻之。

translations.literal: When he was in charge of drafting edicts and patents of nobility, some offered coins in reward; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When drafting edicts and patents of nobility, he firmly declined any payment offered in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 士大夫重其學行，稱為「南屏先生」。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials valued his learning and conduct and called him "Master Nanping."
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials respected his learning and conduct and called him "Master Nanping."

sentences.zh: 王英，字時彥，金溪人。

translations.literal: Wang Ying, styled Shiyan, was a native of Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ying, whose style was Shiyan, came from Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年進士。

translations.literal: Presented scholar in the second year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the second year of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，讀書文淵閣。

translations.literal: Selected as a Hanlin Bachelor, he studied in the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a Hanlin bachelor, he studied in the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 帝察其慎密，令與王直書機密文字。

translations.literal: The Emperor observed his caution and discretion and ordered him together with Wang Zhi to write confidential documents.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noted his discretion and ordered him and Wang Zhi to draft confidential documents.

sentences.zh: 與修《太祖實錄》，授翰林院修撰，進侍讀。

translations.literal: He took part in compiling the Veritable Records of Taizu, was appointed Hanlin Compiler, and advanced to Reader.
translations.idiomatic: He helped compile the Veritable Records of the founding emperor, was appointed a Hanlin compiler, and was promoted to reader.

sentences.zh: 英端凝持重，歷仕四朝。

translations.literal: Ying was dignified, composed, and weighty, and served through four reigns.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was dignified and grave in bearing and served through four reigns.

sentences.zh: 在翰林四十余年，屢為會試考官，朝廷制作多出其手，四方求銘誌碑記者不絕。

translations.literal: He was in the Hanlin Academy more than forty years, repeatedly served as examiner for the metropolitan examination, and much of the court's compositions came from his hand; from all quarters those seeking inscriptions, eulogies, and stele records never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He spent more than forty years in the Hanlin Academy, served repeatedly as metropolitan examiner, and much of the court's official writing came from his hand; requests for epitaphs, eulogies, and commemorative inscriptions never ceased.

sentences.zh: 性直諒，好規人過，三楊皆不喜，故不得柄用。

translations.literal: By nature he was direct and sincere, fond of admonishing others' faults; the Three Yangs all disliked him, and therefore he did not gain control of power.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was frank and sincere and fond of correcting others' faults; the Three Yangs all disliked him, and so he never gained real authority.

sentences.zh: 裕後累官四川按察使。

translations.literal: His son Yu afterward rose through offices to Surveillance Commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu later rose to Surveillance Commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 錢習禮，名幹，以字行，吉水人。

translations.literal: Qian Xili, personal name Gan, was known by his style; he was a native of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Xili, whose personal name was Gan but who was known by his style, came from Jishui.

sentences.zh: 永樂九年進士。

translations.literal: Presented scholar in the ninth year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the ninth year of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，尋授檢討。

translations.literal: Selected as a Hanlin Bachelor, he was soon appointed Reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a Hanlin bachelor, he was soon appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 習禮與練子寧姻戚。

translations.literal: Xili was related by marriage to Lian Zining.
translations.idiomatic: Xili was related by marriage to Lian Zining.

sentences.zh: 既仕，鄉人以奸黨持之，恒惴惴。

translations.literal: After he took office, people of his district treated him as of the treacherous faction, and he was constantly fearful.
translations.idiomatic: After he entered office, people in his home district treated him as a member of the treacherous faction, and he lived in constant anxiety.

sentences.zh: 楊榮乘間言於帝，帝笑曰：「使子寧在，朕猶當用之，況習禮乎。」

translations.literal: Yang Rong seized an occasion to speak to the Emperor; the Emperor laughed and said: "If Zining were alive, I would still employ him—how much more so Xili."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rong spoke to the emperor when he had the chance; the emperor laughed and said, "If Zining were still alive, I would employ him even now—how much more so Xili."

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，遷侍讀，知制誥，以省親歸。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor took the throne, he was transferred to Reader, put in charge of drafting edicts, and returned home to visit his parents.
translations.idiomatic: When the Renzong emperor came to the throne, Xili was promoted to reader and put in charge of drafting edicts, then returned home on leave to visit his parents.

sentences.zh: 正統九年乞致仕。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhengtong he begged to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhengtong he petitioned to retire.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: It was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 明年，六部侍郎多闕，帝命吏部尚書王直會大臣推舉，而特旨擢習禮於禮部。

translations.literal: The next year many vice ministerships in the Six Ministries were vacant; the Emperor ordered Minister of Personnel Wang Zhi to meet with great ministers for recommendations, while by special edict Xili was promoted to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The following year many vice-ministerial posts in the Six Ministries were vacant; the emperor ordered Minister of Personnel Wang Zhi to consult the senior ministers, while by special edict Xili was promoted to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 習禮力辭。

translations.literal: Xili strenuously declined.
translations.idiomatic: Xili strenuously declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 不允。

translations.literal: It was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not accept his refusal.

sentences.zh: 王振用事，達官多造其門，習禮恥為屈。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen held power; eminent officials mostly visited his gate, but Xili was ashamed to bend.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhen held power, high officials flocked to his door, but Xili was ashamed to humble himself.

sentences.zh: 十二年六月復上章乞骸骨，乃得歸。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twelfth year he again submitted a memorial begging for his old bones, and only then was he able to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twelfth year he submitted another memorial asking to retire, and only then was he allowed to go home.

sentences.zh: 習禮篤行誼，好古秉禮，動有矩則。

translations.literal: Xili was earnest in conduct and friendship, loved antiquity and upheld ritual, and in movement had rules and measure.
translations.idiomatic: Xili was earnest in friendship, loved antiquity and upheld ritual, and in all his conduct observed proper measure.

sentences.zh: 家居十五年卒，年八十有九。

translations.literal: Living at home fifteen years, he died at age eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home for fifteen years and died at the age of eighty-nine.

sentences.zh: 謚文肅。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Wénsù.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Wénsù.

sentences.zh: 周敘，字公敘，吉水人。

translations.literal: Zhou Xu, styled Gongxu, was a native of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xu, whose style was Gongxu, came from Jishui.

sentences.zh: 年十一能詩。

translations.literal: At age eleven he could compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he could already compose poetry.

sentences.zh: 永樂十六年進士。

translations.literal: Presented scholar in the sixteenth year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the sixteenth year of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，作《黃鸚鵡賦》，稱旨，授編修。

translations.literal: Selected as a Hanlin Bachelor, he composed the "Fu on the Yellow Oriole," which pleased the intent, and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a Hanlin bachelor, he composed the "Rhapsody on the Yellow Oriole," which pleased the emperor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 歷官侍讀，直經筵。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Reader and attended the lecture hall.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to reader and served on the imperial lecture staff.

sentences.zh: 正統六年上疏言事，帝嘉納焉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengtong he submitted a memorial on affairs; the Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhengtong he submitted a memorial on state affairs, which the emperor warmly accepted.

sentences.zh: 八年夏又上言：「比天旱，陛下責躬虔禱，而臣下不聞效忠補過之言，徒陳情乞用而已。

translations.literal: In the summer of the eighth year he again spoke: "Recently there has been drought; Your Majesty blames himself and prays devoutly, yet among ministers one does not hear words of loyal service to remedy faults—only pleas of personal feeling begging employment.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the eighth year he memorialized again: "Recently there has been drought; Your Majesty blames yourself and prays devoutly, yet your ministers offer no loyal counsel to remedy faults—only personal pleas begging for appointment.

sentences.zh: 掌銓選者罔論賢否，第循資格。

translations.literal: Those in charge of selection disregard whether men are worthy or not and merely follow seniority.
translations.idiomatic: Those in charge of appointments pay no heed to merit and merely follow seniority.

sentences.zh: 司國計者不問耕桑，惟勤賦斂。

translations.literal: Those who manage the state's accounts do not inquire into farming and sericulture but only press levies.
translations.idiomatic: Those who manage the state's finances do not inquire into farming and sericulture but only press for taxes.

sentences.zh: 軍士困役作，刑罰失重輕，風憲無激揚，言官務緘默。

translations.literal: Soldiers are distressed by corvée labor; punishments lose proper weight and lightness; the censorate has no arousing and promotion; remonstrance officials strive for silence.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers are worn down by labor service; punishments are no longer proportionate; the censorate no longer stirs men to action; and remonstrance officials keep silent.

sentences.zh: 僧道數萬，日耗戶口，流民眾多，莫為矜恤。」

translations.literal: Monks and Daoists number in the tens of thousands, daily draining households; displaced people are many, yet none show pity and relief."
translations.idiomatic: Monks and Daoist priests number in the tens of thousands, daily draining the population; refugees are numerous, yet no one shows them compassion."

sentences.zh: 帝以章示諸大臣。

translations.literal: The Emperor showed the memorial to the great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed the memorial to the senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 王直等皆引罪求罷。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi and others all acknowledged guilt and begged to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi and the others all acknowledged fault and asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 十一年遷南京侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to Lecturing Scholar at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was transferred to lecturing scholar at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 郕王監國，馳疏言：「君父之仇不共戴天，殿下宜臥薪嘗膽，如越之報吳。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Cheng supervised the state, he sent a hurried memorial saying: "The feud between ruler and father admits no living under the same heaven; Your Highness should sleep on brushwood and taste gall, like Yue avenging Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Cheng supervised the state, Xu sent an urgent memorial saying, "The feud with one's sovereign and father admits no compromise; Your Highness should sleep on brushwood and taste gall, as Yue did in preparing to destroy Wu.

sentences.zh: 使智者獻謀，勇者效力，務掃北庭，雪國恥。

translations.literal: Let the wise offer plans and the brave exert strength; strive to sweep the northern court and wash away the nation's shame.
translations.idiomatic: Let the wise offer counsel and the brave exert themselves; strive to sweep the northern court clean and wipe away the nation's disgrace.

sentences.zh: 先遣辯士，卑詞重幣乞還鑾輿，暫為君父屈。」

translations.literal: First send eloquent envoys with humble words and heavy gifts to beg the return of the imperial carriage, temporarily bending for ruler and father."
translations.idiomatic: First send eloquent envoys with humble words and rich gifts to beg the return of the imperial carriage, bending for the moment to the needs of sovereign and father."

sentences.zh: 因條上勵剛明、親經史、修軍政、選賢才、安民心、廣言路、謹微漸、修庶政八事。

translations.literal: He thereupon set forth eight items: encourage firmness and clarity, draw near to the classics and histories, repair military administration, select worthy talent, settle the people's hearts, broaden the path of remonstrance, guard against gradual encroachment, and repair ordinary government.
translations.idiomatic: He then set forth eight recommendations: encourage firmness and clarity, study the classics and histories, restore military administration, select worthy talent, reassure the people, broaden the path of remonstrance, guard against gradual encroachment, and repair ordinary government.

sentences.zh: 王嘉納之。

translations.literal: The Prince praised and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: The prince praised and accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年又請復午朝，日接大臣，咨諏治道。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingtai he again asked to restore the noon audience, daily receiving great ministers and consulting on the way of governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingtai he again asked to restore the noon audience, to receive senior ministers daily and consult them on governance.

sentences.zh: 經筵之余，召文學從臣講論政事，並詔天下臣民直言時政缺失。

translations.literal: Beyond the lecture hall, he summoned literary attendants to discuss government affairs, and also ordered all officials and people under Heaven to speak plainly of present political shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the lecture sessions he summoned literary attendants to discuss government affairs, and also ordered officials and subjects throughout the empire to speak plainly about present failings in policy.

sentences.zh: 帝因詔求言。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon issued an edict seeking words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon issued an edict calling for candid counsel.

sentences.zh: 敘負氣節，篤行誼。

translations.literal: Xu possessed moral backbone and was earnest in conduct and friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Xu possessed strong moral backbone and was earnest in friendship.

sentences.zh: 曾祖以立，在元時以宋、遼、金三史體例未當，欲重修。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yili, in Yuan times because the institutional forms of the histories of Song, Liao, and Jin were improper, wished to recompile them.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yili, during the Yuan, believed the institutional arrangements of the histories of Song, Liao, and Jin were unsatisfactory and wished to recompile them.

sentences.zh: 敘思繼先誌，正統末，請於朝。

translations.literal: Xu thought to continue his ancestor's aim; at the end of Zhengtong he requested it at court.
translations.idiomatic: Xu wished to continue his ancestor's project; late in the Zhengtong reign he petitioned the court.

sentences.zh: 詔許自撰，銓次數年，未及成而卒。

translations.literal: An edict permitted him to compile on his own; for several years he arranged and ordered the material, but before it was finished he died.
translations.idiomatic: An edict permitted him to compile the work on his own; he worked on arranging the material for several years but died before it was finished.

sentences.zh: 同邑劉儼，字宣化。

translations.literal: Liu Yan of the same district, styled Xuanhua.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan of the same district, whose style was Xuanhua.

sentences.zh: 正統七年進士第一。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhengtong he ranked first among presented scholars.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhengtong he ranked first in the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 歷官太常少卿。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 景泰中，典順天鄉試，黜大學士陳循、王文子，幾得危禍。

translations.literal: In the Jingtai reign he presided over the Shuntian provincial examination and failed the sons of Grand Secretaries Chen Xun and Wang Wen, nearly bringing disaster on himself.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingtai reign he presided over the Shuntian provincial examination and failed the sons of Grand Secretaries Chen Xun and Wang Wen, nearly bringing disaster upon himself.

sentences.zh: 詳《高谷傳》。

translations.literal: See the biography of Gao Gu.
translations.idiomatic: See the biography of Gao Gu.

sentences.zh: 天順初，改掌翰林院事，卒官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun he was changed to direct affairs of the Hanlin Academy and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianshun reign he was put in charge of the Hanlin Academy and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部侍郎，謚文介。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Vice Minister of Rites, with the posthumous title Wénjiè.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Vice Minister of Rites and given the posthumous title Wénjiè.

sentences.zh: 儼立朝正直，居鄉亦有令德雲。

translations.literal: Yan stood upright at court, and in his district also had fine virtue, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was upright at court and, it is said, possessed fine virtue in his home district as well.

sentences.zh: 柯潛，字孟時，莆田人。

translations.literal: Ke Qian, styled Mengshi, was a native of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Qian, whose style was Mengshi, came from Putian.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年舉進士第一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingtai he ranked first among presented scholars.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingtai he ranked first in the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 歷洗馬。

translations.literal: He served as Groom.
translations.idiomatic: He served as groom in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 天順初，遷尚寶少卿，兼修撰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Treasures, concurrently Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianshun reign he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Treasures while also serving as compiler.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，以舊宮僚擢翰林學士。

translations.literal: When the Xianzong Emperor took the throne, as an old household officer he was promoted to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianzong emperor came to the throne, he was promoted to Hanlin academician on account of his earlier service in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 《英宗實錄》成，進少詹事。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of the Yingzong Emperor were finished, he was advanced to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After the Veritable Records of the Yingzong emperor were completed, he was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 慈懿太后之喪，潛與修撰羅璟上章，請合葬裕陵。

translations.literal: At the funeral of the Empress Dowager Ciyi, Qian together with Compiler Luo Jing submitted a memorial asking that she be buried together at Yuling.
