translations.idiomatic: At the funeral of Empress Dowager Ciyi, Qian and Compiler Luo Jing submitted a memorial asking that she be buried with the Yingzong emperor at Yuling.

sentences.zh: 廷臣相繼爭。

translations.literal: Court ministers disputed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers disputed the matter one after another.

sentences.zh: 未報。

translations.literal: No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: No reply came from the throne.

sentences.zh: 潛曰：「朝廷大事，臣子大節，舍是奚所用心。」

translations.literal: Qian said: "Great affairs of the court, great integrity of ministers—apart from these, upon what else should the mind be set?"
translations.idiomatic: Qian said, "Great affairs of state and the great integrity of a minister—apart from these, upon what else should one's mind be set?"

sentences.zh: 與璟皆再疏爭，竟得如禮。

translations.literal: He and Jing both memorialized again in dispute, and in the end it was done according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He and Jing both submitted further memorials in protest, and in the end the burial was carried out according to proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 連遭父母喪，詔起為祭酒，固乞終制。

translations.literal: He suffered in succession the mourning for both parents; an edict summoned him back to be Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, but he firmly begged to complete the full mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: After losing both parents in succession, he was summoned back by edict to serve as chancellor of the Directorate of Education, but he firmly asked to complete the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 潛邃於文學，性高介。

translations.literal: Qian was deep in literary learning and by nature lofty and independent.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was deeply learned in literature and by nature lofty and aloof.

sentences.zh: 為學士時，即院中後圃構清風亭，鑿池蒔芙蓉，植二柏於後堂，人稱其亭為「柯亭」，柏為「學士柏」。

translations.literal: When he was an Academician, in the rear garden of the academy he built the Clear Wind Pavilion, dug a pool and planted hibiscus, and set two cypresses behind the main hall; people called his pavilion "Ke Pavilion" and the cypresses "Academician Cypresses."
translations.idiomatic: While serving as academician, he built the Clear Wind Pavilion in the academy's rear garden, dug a pool and planted hibiscus, and set two cypresses behind the main hall; people called the pavilion "Ke Pavilion" and the trees "Academician Cypresses."

sentences.zh: 院中有井，學士劉定之所浚也。

translations.literal: In the academy there was a well that Academician Liu Ding had excavated.
translations.idiomatic: The academy also had a well excavated by Academician Liu Ding.

sentences.zh: 柯亭、劉井，翰林中以為美談雲。

translations.literal: Ke Pavilion and Liu's Well were regarded in the Hanlin as fine tales, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Pavilion and Liu's Well were regarded in the Hanlin Academy as cherished stories.

sentences.zh: 羅璟，字明仲，泰和人。

translations.literal: Luo Jing, styled Mingzhong, was a native of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Jing, whose style was Mingzhong, came from Taihe.

sentences.zh: 天順末，進士及第。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianshun he passed the presented scholar examination with highest honors.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Tianshun reign he passed the metropolitan examination with highest honors.

sentences.zh: 授編修，進修撰。

translations.literal: He was appointed Compiler and advanced to Senior Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed compiler and later promoted to senior compiler.

sentences.zh: 預修《宋元通鑒綱目》。

translations.literal: He took part in compiling the Comprehensive Mirror of Song and Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He helped compile the Comprehensive Mirror of Song and Yuan.

sentences.zh: 累官洗馬。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Groom.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of groom in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 孝宗為太子，簡侍講讀。

translations.literal: When the Xiaozong Emperor was heir apparent, he was selected to attend in lecture and reading.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiaozong emperor was heir apparent, Jing was chosen to serve on his lecture staff.

sentences.zh: 母喪歸。

translations.literal: On his mother's mourning he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 璟與尚書尹旻子侍講龍同娶於孔氏。

translations.literal: Jing and Minister Yin Min's son, Lecturer Long, both married women of the Kong clan.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Lecturer Long, son of Minister Yin Min, both married women of the Kong clan.

sentences.zh: 旻得罪，李孜省指璟為旻黨，調南京禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Min fell into guilt, Li Zisheng pointed to Jing as of Min's faction and transferred him to Departmental Director in the Ministry of Rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When Min fell from power, Li Zisheng denounced Jing as one of Min's faction and transferred him to departmental director in the Ministry of Rites at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嗣位，王恕等言璟才，乃授福建提學副使。

translations.literal: When the Xiaozong Emperor succeeded to the throne, Wang Shu and others spoke of Jing's talent, and he was appointed Vice Commissioner of Education in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiaozong emperor succeeded to the throne, Wang Shu and others spoke of Jing's ability, and he was appointed vice commissioner of education in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 弘治五年召為南京祭酒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Hongzhi he was summoned to be Chancellor of the Directorate of Education at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Hongzhi he was summoned to serve as chancellor of the Directorate of Education at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒。

translations.literal: After a long time he died.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he died.

sentences.zh: 孔公恂，字宗文，先聖五十八世孫也。

translations.literal: Kong Gongxun, styled Zongwen, was a fifty-eighth-generation descendant of the Former Sage.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Gongxun, whose style was Zongwen, was a fifty-eighth-generation descendant of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 景泰五年舉會試，聞母疾，不赴廷對。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jingtai he passed the metropolitan examination; hearing his mother was ill, he did not attend the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jingtai he passed the metropolitan examination, but on hearing that his mother was ill he did not attend the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 帝以問禮部，具言其故，乃遣使召之。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked the Ministry of Rites, which set forth the reason in full, and then sent an envoy to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor inquired of the Ministry of Rites, which explained the circumstances in full, and then sent an envoy to summon him.

sentences.zh: 日且午，不及備試卷，命翰林院給以筆劄。

translations.literal: The day was nearly noon and he had no time to prepare examination papers; he was ordered to be given brush and paper by the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: It was nearly noon and he had no time to prepare his examination papers, so the Hanlin Academy was ordered to supply him with writing materials.

sentences.zh: 登第，即丁母憂歸。

translations.literal: He passed the grade and at once entered mourning for his mother and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examination, but immediately entered mourning for his mother and returned home.

sentences.zh: 衍聖公孔彥縉卒，孫弘緒幼弱，詔遣禮部郎治喪，公恂理其家事。

translations.literal: The Duke Who Expands Sagehood Kong Yanjin died; his grandson Hongxu was young and weak; an edict sent a Secretary in the Ministry of Rites to manage the funeral, and Gongxun handled his household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke Who Expands Sagehood Kong Yanjin died, his grandson Hongxu was still a child; an edict sent a secretary in the Ministry of Rites to manage the funeral, and Gongxun handled the household affairs.

sentences.zh: 天順初，授禮科給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun he was appointed Supervising Secretary in the Rites Section.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianshun reign he was appointed supervising secretary in the Rites Section.

sentences.zh: 弘緒已襲封，大學士李賢妻以女，公恂因得交於賢。

translations.literal: Hongxu had already inherited the enfeoffment; Grand Secretary Li Xian gave him his daughter in marriage, and through this Gongxun was able to form ties with Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxu had already inherited the title; Grand Secretary Li Xian gave him his daughter in marriage, and through this Gongxun came to know Xian.

sentences.zh: 賢言：「公恂，大聖人後；

translations.literal: Xian said: "Gongxun is a descendant of the Great Sage;
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "Gongxun is a descendant of the Great Sage;

sentences.zh: 贊善司馬恂，宋大賢溫國公光後。

translations.literal: Tutor Sima Xun is a descendant of the great Song worthy, Wenguo Duke Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Tutor Sima Xun is a descendant of the great Song worthy Sima Guang, Duke of Wenguo.

sentences.zh: 宜輔導太子。」

translations.literal: They ought to tutor the heir apparent."
translations.idiomatic: Both are fit to tutor the heir apparent."

sentences.zh: 帝喜。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 同日超拜少詹事，侍東宮講讀。

translations.literal: That same day he was abruptly promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent to attend the Eastern Palace in lecture and reading.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was abruptly promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and appointed to lecture the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 入語孝肅皇后曰：「吾今日得聖賢子孫為汝子傅。」

translations.literal: Entering, he said to the Empress Dowager Xiaosu: "Today I have obtained descendants of sages to be tutors for your son."
translations.idiomatic: He went in and told Empress Dowager Xiaosu, "Today I have obtained descendants of sages to serve as tutors for your son."

sentences.zh: 孝肅皇后者，憲宗生母，方以皇貴妃有寵。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager Xiaosu was the Xianzong Emperor's birth mother and was then favored as Imperial Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xiaosu was the Xianzong emperor's birth mother and was then favored as imperial noble consort.

sentences.zh: 於是具冠服拜謝，宮中傳以為盛事雲。

translations.literal: Thereupon she put on cap and robes and bowed in thanks; within the palace it was passed around as a great occasion, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: She thereupon donned full ceremonial dress and bowed in thanks; within the palace the event was celebrated as a great occasion.

sentences.zh: 憲宗嗣位，改公恂大理左少卿。

translations.literal: When the Xianzong Emperor succeeded to the throne, Gongxun was changed to Left Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianzong emperor succeeded to the throne, Gongxun was transferred to Left Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 公恂言不通法律，乃復少詹事。

translations.literal: Gongxun said he did not understand law, and was therefore restored to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Gongxun said he did not understand law and was therefore restored to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 成化二年上章言兵事，諸武臣嘩然，給事御史交章駁之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua he submitted a memorial on military affairs; the military officials clamored, and Supervising Secretaries and Censors submitted successive memorials refuting him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chenghua he submitted a memorial on military affairs; the military officials protested loudly, and supervising secretaries and censors submitted successive memorials refuting him.

sentences.zh: 下獄，謫漢陽知府。

translations.literal: He was put in prison and banished to be prefect of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was imprisoned and banished to serve as prefect of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 未至，丁父憂。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, he entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived, he entered mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，商輅請復建言得罪者官，乃還故秩，涖南京詹事府。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, Shang Luo asked to restore to office those who had offended by offering counsel, and Gongxun returned to his former rank and went to the Household of the Heir Apparent at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, Shang Luo petitioned to restore officials who had been punished for offering counsel, and Gongxun was restored to his former rank and took up office at the heir apparent's household in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒。

translations.literal: After a long time he died.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he died.

sentences.zh: 司馬恂，字恂如，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Sima Xun, styled Xunru, was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xun, whose style was Xunru, came from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 正統末，由舉人擢刑科給事中，累遷少詹事。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengtong, from Presented Scholar he was promoted to Supervising Secretary in the Punishments Section and rose to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Zhengtong reign he was promoted from presented scholar to supervising secretary in the Punishments Section and rose to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，命兼國子祭酒。

translations.literal: When the Xianzong Emperor was established, he was ordered concurrently to be Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianzong emperor came to the throne, he was ordered also to serve as chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈禮部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Left Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Left Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 恂強記、敦厚，與物無忤，居官無所表見。

translations.literal: Xun had a strong memory and was thick and steady, at odds with nothing, and in office showed nothing particular.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had a powerful memory and was steadfast and mild, at odds with no one, yet in office left no particular mark.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：「建文之初，修尊賢敬老之節。

translations.literal: The commentator says: "At the beginning of Jianwen, the observance of honoring the worthy and respecting the aged was cultivated.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: "At the beginning of the Jianwen reign, the court cultivated the practice of honoring the worthy and respecting the aged.

sentences.zh: 董倫以宿儒見重，雖寡所表見，當非茍焉已也。

translations.literal: Dong Lun was valued as a longstanding scholar; although he showed little in particular, he surely was not one to stop at mere perfunctoriness.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Lun was valued as a senior scholar; though he left little in the way of visible achievement, he can hardly have been a man who stopped at mere perfunctoriness.

sentences.zh: 儀智父子仍世以儒術進，從容輔導，蓋其賢哉。

translations.literal: Yi Zhi, father and son, through successive generations advanced by Confucian learning and calmly assisted and instructed—how worthy they were!
translations.idiomatic: Yi Zhi and his son advanced through successive generations by Confucian learning and calmly guided their charges—how worthy they were!

sentences.zh: 鄒濟諸人，以宮僚被遇而讒構不免。

translations.literal: Zou Ji and the others, favored as household officers, could not escape slander and plotting.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Ji and his colleagues, favored as officers of the heir apparent's household, could not escape slander and intrigue.

sentences.zh: 陳濟輩起布衣，列禁近而善始終，固有幸不幸歟。

translations.literal: Chen Ji and his kind rose from commoner status, entered the forbidden proximity, and had good beginnings and ends—surely there is fortune and misfortune?
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ji and his like rose from commoner status to serve in the inner court and managed good beginnings and ends—surely fortune and misfortune both played their part?

sentences.zh: 二周、王英、錢習禮、周敘、柯潛謙和直諒，各著其美，蓋皆異於浮華博習之徒矣。

translations.literal: The two Zhous, Wang Ying, Qian Xili, Zhou Xu, and Ke Qian were modest, harmonious, direct, and sincere, each displaying his excellence—they were all unlike those of flashy display and broad but shallow learning.
translations.idiomatic: The two Zhous, Wang Ying, Qian Xili, Zhou Xu, and Ke Qian were modest, harmonious, frank, and sincere, each displaying his own excellence—they were all unlike men of flashy display and broad but shallow learning.
